title: Felix and the Sigil Anew
premise: Oscar Iversen, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has hidden their magic for fifteen years in Grayhollow, a city that outlawed it — until the border wards collapse and the stars go out on the same night. Dragged back into the old war by Felix, a runaway court-scribe whose soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain as collateral for his family's debts, Oscar must gather the scattered remnants of their found family and descend to bargain with the Sigil Anew, the living seal that feeds on sworn souls. To free Felix, Oscar must break their own oath — the very thing that has kept them alive and sane — and offer the Sigil something it has never been given: a vow freely unmade. In the end, Oscar survives the breaking but loses their swordspeech forever, the stars return dimmer but honest, and the found family they nearly destroyed chooses to stay.
about_author: Beatrix Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken legal contracts and swears it changed how she writes about magic. She lives near a mountain she refuses to name and writes only after dark.

chapters.title: Charms for Small Coin
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Fifteen years of hiding: Oscar sells luck-knots and fever-charms in Grayhollow's night market, oath-bound and magic-starved, watching a young scribe named Felix buy a charm he cannot afford. The beat is weary tenderness — survival as habit, not life.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The border wards shatter at moonrise and every star vanishes; panic floods the city. Felix flees the chancery carrying a stolen ledger that names him as collateral, and collides with Oscar in the dark streets. Beat: terror sharpening into desperate resolve.

chapters.title: An Oath Refuses to Sleep
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The fallen wards wake Oscar's dormant swordspeech, burning down their arm like remembered fire. They take in Felix, recognize the ledger's seal as the Sigil Anew's mark, and realize the boy's soul is already half-claimed. Beat: dread and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Company of the Broken
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Oscar seeks out old comrades: Maren, a ward-smith turned drunkard; Tallow, a thief-priest of a banned god; and Brannic, who betrayed them fifteen years ago and now begs to help. Beat: brittle reunion, found family reassembling around an old wound.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Promised
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confesses: his family sold his soul to the under-court to erase their debts, and the ledger proves the sale is binding at the next new moon. Maren reads the contract's true clause — the Sigil must be paid willingly or it takes the whole city. Beat: guilt curdling into determination.

chapters.title: Raiders of the Warded Road
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The company leaves Grayhollow through the collapsed wards, ambushed by hollow-men — soulless enforcers of the under-court hunting Felix. Oscar draws the sword-speech for the first time in years and it costs them blood and memory. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by price.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Tallow's POV. They shelter in a village where the Sigil's hunger has eaten every spoken memory; an old woman mistakes Felix for her son. Tallow's forbidden god answers a prayer for the first time in decades. Beat: grief made communal, faith kindling.

chapters.title: Brannic's Confession
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. By the fire, Brannic admits he sold the company out fifteen years ago to save his sister from the same court that now holds Felix. Oscar refuses forgiveness but accepts his sword. Beat: bitter honesty, the first crack in old betrayal.

chapters.title: The Mountain Opens Its Mouth
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They reach the mountain gate, a wound in the rock breathing cold, guarded by a toll of names: each traveler must surrender one true memory to enter. Maren gives up her wedding day. Beat: sacrifice as toll, love measured in loss.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Beneath the mountain: a city of bone-white lanterns where the sold souls serve as clerks in an endless bureaucracy of debt. Felix finds his own file and sees what he will become if the new moon passes. Beat: horror of paperwork-as-damnation.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The company petitions the under-court's magistrates, ancient souls wearing borrowed faces, who offer a trade: Felix's freedom for Oscar's oath, freely surrendered. Oscar stalls, sensing the trap inside the gift. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: A Debt Called Friendship
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix learns Oscar once swore the same oath to save this same court a prisoner — and failed, which is why the Sigil hungers still. Feeling like a replacement for a ghost, Felix runs. Beat: jealousy and self-worth colliding.

chapters.title: The Sigil Anew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Deep in the court's heart, they meet the Sigil itself: a living seal of interlocked vows, starved since the stars went out because it fed on starlight-sworn oaths. It shows Oscar the future if unpaid — Grayhollow hollowed like the village. Beat: awe and revulsion entwined.

chapters.title: What Maren Broke
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren discovers the magistrates plan to take Felix AND keep Oscar's oath, voiding the bargain. She begins quietly rewiring the court's ward-lattice with smuggled tools, buying time she may not survive to use. Beat: quiet heroism, hands shaking.

chapters.title: Tallow's Bargain with a Banned God
chapters.summary: Tallow's POV. Tallow trades his priesthood — his god's last anchor in the world — for one miracle: a door out of the mountain that opens only for the willing. The god agrees, weeping. Beat: devotion spent like coin, faith as currency.

chapters.title: New Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The new moon arrives above; below, the court convenes to finalize Felix's claim. Felix returns voluntarily, choosing to face the Sigil rather than let it take the city — mirroring Oscar's old failure with courage instead of desperation. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Oath
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax begins: before the assembled court, Oscar speaks their oath aloud and then unswears it word by word, offering the Sigil a vow freely unmade — the payment it was built to receive and never got. The court screams; the lattice shakes. Beat: terrible liberation.

chapters.title: Hollow-Men at the Gate
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. As the Sigil convulses, the magistrates unleash every hollow-man to stop the escape. Brannic holds the stair alone so the others can run, redeeming fifteen years in one stand, and falls — but his death breaks the toll-of-names forever. Beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: The Starlight Clause
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Climax resolves: with the oath unmade, the Sigil releases all claimed souls including Felix's — but demands a new anchor. Maren's rewired lattice offers it the freed memories of the village, letting it feed on returned truth instead of stolen souls. Beat: cleverness as salvation.

chapters.title: Out of the Mountain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The company climbs toward Tallow's door, pursued by collapsing courts, and steps through into starlight — real stars, dim but returning, as the Sigil's release lets light back into the sky. Oscar reaches for their swordspeech and finds silence where it lived. Beat: victory laced with permanent loss.

chapters.title: Grayhollow Remembers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The city wakes to returned stars and returned memories; the outlawed magic is debated openly for the first time in a generation. Oscar, powerless now, teaches charm-craft as plain craft, and the council asks them to help write the new wards' laws. Beat: quiet rebuilding, purpose reforged.

chapters.title: The Family We Chose
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Epilogue: a year later, the found family gathers in Oscar's shop — Maren sober and building, Tallow godless but content, Brannic's name carved over the door. Felix, soul his own, signs his first honest contract: apprenticeship. Final beat: home is not given, it is kept.
